messages:
alex: Quick signal — profiler shows sustained KV cache memory growth on the long-context load (16k tokens). Fragmentation ratio drifting up to ~0.46 after ~1hr, eviction rate spike around same time.

maya: Details? flamegraph / alloc traces?

alex: Pasted the snapshot from the canary: 
```
kv_frag_ratio=0.463
total_kv_mem=13.2GB
wasted=6.1GB
evict_ops/sec=120
long_context_pct=0.12
active_shards=48
```

maya: Yikes. Is this tied to the buddy allocator change we rolled last week?

liam: I ran a quick local repro with a synthetic 16k-stream. Looks like buddy split threshold + current block_size = many tiny free holes after partial evictions. Those holes aren't being reused efficiently.

alex: Thinking out loud: add a background compaction scheduler that coalesces adjacent free blocks and selectively relocates cold entries into larger slabs. Triggering heuristics: frag_ratio > 0.35 for >60s and eviction_rate > baseline.

maya: Sounds reasonable but worried about CPU noise on heavy traffic. We should throttle compaction (budgeted ms) and prefer run during batching idle windows.

liam: Another lever: per-model block_size/profile. Large-sequence models allocate bigger KV entries; small chat models waste space with big blocks. Dynamically chosen block size might reduce fragmentation.

alex: Agreed. Proposed minimal scheduler prototype: prioritise shards by wasted_bytes, skip shards with high eviction churn (to avoid moving hot entries).

sarah: Can we identify per-shard culprit models in traces? I'll add fine-grained tracepoints so we can map wasted bytes -> model id / route.

ops-bot: deploy queued: kv-alloc-trace enabled on canary-3 :rocket:

alex: Prototype scheduler sketch:
```
// heuristics: frag_ratio, evict_rate, cpu_idle, consecutive_free_runs
if frag_ratio > FRAG_TH && cpu_idle_pct > CPU_TH:
  for shard in shards_sorted_by_waste:
    if shard.eviction_rate > EVICT_TH: // avoid hot
      continue
    compact(shard, budget_ms)
```

maya: Important: compaction must be LRU-aware so we don't relocate hot entries. Also, prefer incremental coalescing instead of big moves. Add a max_moved_bytes/sec cap.

liam: We should also try a simpler experiment first: bump default block_size for long-context models to 16k and compare fragmentation over 6h run. If that moves the needle, we avoid complexity.

alex: Good call. I'll run both experiments in parallel on canary: (A) compaction scheduler, (B) block_size bump. Keep everything else constant.

maya: Add telemetry: compaction_count, bytes_coalesced, entries_moved, compaction_time_ms, pre_frag_ratio, post_frag_ratio. Dashboards needed.

sarah: I'll own the trace run tonight and add those metrics + allocation histograms. Also capturing KV hit latency distribution pre/post compaction.

alex: Also adding safety: skip compaction if cpu_usage > 70% or if tail-latency SLO > target. We don't want compaction to regress latencies.

liam: Don't forget to expose knobs: max_moved_bytes_per_sec, compaction_budget_ms, frag_threshold, min_free_run_seconds. Make them runtime flags for quick tuning.

maya: Sounds good. Plan: deploy tracing + block_size bump to canary-3 now, schedule compaction PR for review tomorrow. We'll run 6h A/B with long-context generator, then reconvene. :thumbsup:

sarah: Thanks — will post the first trace later today. tagging @eng-sre for dashboard watch.

alex: I'll draft the PR and prototype scheduler logs. Also trying a hybrid: coalesce holes first (cheap) then move cold entries only if coalescing doesn't free enough contiguous space.

liam: One more thought: we might use a tiny per-shard freelist compaction window that only runs between batches to reduce interference with token generation.

maya: OK. If canary numbers look good, we can stage rollout to dedicated and then private with a longer bake.

sarah: Reconvene after the canary run — thanks team.
